atomicity.reason: One shall-clause and one obligation: cap the published permitted discharge power so the 10 s average pack discharge current stays at or below 250 A. The sentence that a short peak stays available is the negative case of that limit and the so-it-does-not-heat-up clause is its rationale (same pattern as the inrush sentence of REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT), so neither is a second obligation.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: the published quantity, the measured quantity, the window, the threshold and the purpose are all stated in plain domain terms, and permitted discharge power and the derating range are used as in the story and REQ_POWER_DERATING, so no adjacent requirement has to be read to follow it.

feasibility.reason: A windowed current budget on the 1 ms shunt measurement feeding a published power cap is standard BMS practice and needs no new technology. Nothing stated contradicts it: 250 A averaged over 10 s sits below the 350 A for 100 ms trip of REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT, so the peak it leaves available is bounded by that trip, and as a cap it composes with REQ_POWER_DERATING and REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE by taking the lower value (which is what the architecture does). That the actual current follows the limit depends on the vehicle honouring it; that is the standard allocation for a published limit and is scored under verifiability, not here.

parent_fit.reason: Directly implements the towing sentence of the story: even under sustained full load the pack never draws more than its cells are rated to deliver continuously, so it does not heat into the range where drive power is cut back. It turns that into a concrete bound (10 s average at or below 250 A) and covers a distinct part of the story; the cooling and heating requests, the temperature ramp, the actuator fail-safe and the spread warning belong to siblings.

unambiguity.reason: The core reading is single: a sliding 10 s window and a 250 A ceiling applied as a cap on the published power, so it composes with the temperature ramp and the 30 % fall-back by the lower value without a precedence clash. Open points that do not change that core: short peak is undefined (an instantaneous 250 A cap would satisfy the shall-clause yet contradict the sentence that a short peak stays available) and the real ceiling on a peak is the 350 A for 100 ms trip of REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT, which this text never mentions; the sign convention for regenerative current is unstated; and the clause that the pack does not heat up into the range where its drive power has to be cut back reads as an outcome the BMS ensures although a current limit alone cannot guarantee a temperature (ambient, cooling), so its normative status is unclear.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define short peak numerically (or mark that sentence as non-normative), name the averaging convention (net or discharge-only), and phrase the heat-up clause as the reason for the limit rather than as a result it guarantees.

verifiability.reason: Threshold (250 A), unit and window (any 10 s interval, i.e. sliding) are explicit, so a recorded shunt trace gives an objective pass/fail. Three details a test needs are missing: the sentence that a short peak stays available gives no magnitude or duration (and a pure cap is trivially met by publishing 0 %, so the stays-available half is untestable); the success condition is the actual pack current, which the BMS only influences through the published limit, yet the condition under which it must hold (a consumer that follows the limit, and how quickly) is not stated; and whether regenerative current is netted in the average is not stated.
verifiability.suggestion: State the test condition (for example while the vehicle draws no more than the published permitted discharge power); quantify the peak that must remain available (current and duration, bounded by the 350 A for 100 ms trip of REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT) or relabel that sentence as rationale; state the sign convention for the average.

summary: A well-targeted single-obligation requirement that implements the towing case of the story with an explicit 250 A / 10 s bound, held back by an unquantified sentence on short peaks, an unstated condition under which the actual-current outcome must hold, and an unstated averaging convention for regenerative current.
